[K/N][stdlib] Make k.math.round independent from global rounding mode
body.body:
Currently a call to `fesetround`, even made outside of Kotlin (from C/Obj-C/Swift/whatever), can change the behavior of `kotlin.math.round` in a thread. I'm pretty sure it's not intentional.

The fix is to avoid `rint` and use `roundeven` according to the [function contract]. Unfortunately `roundeven` is:
- only converted to CPU instructions on arm64 or x86 when built with SSE 4.1 (not currently the case)
- not present in the libc versions used on Linux & Windows.

That's why a fallback has been introduced. The fallback only applies on *Arm32 and *X64 platforms. In the latter case only when running on a CPU without SSE 4.1.

An even faster implementation is possible but is harder to follow/maintain. It still stays an option in the future if the rounding performance would have to be improved on the above platforms.

This PR also adds some rounding test cases verifying:
- zero sign preservation
- signaling NaN quieting and NaN payload preservation

Not committed artifacts:
- [Benchmark]
- [Brute force acceptance test][Acceptance test]

[Acceptance Test]: https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34173416/KT-90103-acceptance.cpp
[Benchmark]: https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34142911/FloatingPointRoundingBenchmark.kt.zip
[function contract]: https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/blob/baed79215d93235ad7b3d6cfaffa9dd7020864ee/libraries/stdlib/common/src/kotlin/MathH.kt#L376

^KT-90103 Fixed

body.title: [Build] Add Kotlin Build Tools libraries
body.body:
This pull request introduces and documents a new structure for Gradle-independent Kotlin Build Tools libraries, which are shared by multiple build tool integrations (such as KGP, Maven, JPS, kotlin-toolchain, and Bazel). It adds comprehensive guidelines, ownership, conventions, and review rules for these libraries, ensuring maintainability and consistency across the repository. The changes also update documentation and code ownership to reflect this new organization.

**Key changes:**

**1. Introduction of Kotlin Build Tools libraries**
- Added the `build-tools/libraries/` directory, with a detailed `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` explaining the purpose, layout, usage, and rules for Gradle-independent libraries shared by build tool integrations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-74209963b1935accbfee2e442b3504262f2af774b931f9a13ff68162e455be9cR1-R39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d16d22b9e186d9a0b608b8ed03faaa10bf2e9c05ae2644008125696a0fcde578R1-R160)
- Created `library-rules.md` with review rules and best practices for these libraries, covering dependencies, API boundaries, testing, and documentation.

**2. Build conventions and tooling**
- Added the `kotlin-build-tools-library` convention plugin, with its own `README.md`, to standardize setup, compilation, publishing, and testing for all libraries under `build-tools/libraries`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7a9be949b05b79df8969b1844f1c8906faaebb2c1310ec0d3bb9aa8d7b29c733R1-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f75ed89b8c1ad49c671195f25c7cb7048b2c5b49a88230e2276a49773fa9dbb2R8)

**3. Documentation and guidelines updates**
- Updated `.ai/guidelines.md` to reference the new libraries, their purpose, and their place in the project structure and ownership table. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a1175a209c714f16cc6e2d07c01f73ea3f4b70520308b9a984b51f7c76d06a02R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a1175a209c714f16cc6e2d07c01f73ea3f4b70520308b9a984b51f7c76d06a02R48)
- Updated `libraries/tools/kotlin-gradle-plugin/AGENTS.md` to direct contributors to move Gradle-independent logic to these libraries and reference their documentation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-247c6dc6387dcafd67dfa843f9efe17b17cdc8994de2d99569a966e230818b5eR25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-247c6dc6387dcafd67dfa843f9efe17b17cdc8994de2d99569a966e230818b5eR78-R81)

**4. Code ownership and domain mapping**
- Added code ownership rules for `build-tools/libraries/` and related convention plugins in `.space/CODEOWNERS`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d4b582a5511506f5bbc658a76d5dccba229aa175ca7f822350f0dc974b6680a7R355) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d4b582a5511506f5bbc658a76d5dccba229aa175ca7f822350f0dc974b6680a7R479)
- Updated domain mapping files (`repo/domains.dump.txt`, `repo/domains.yaml`) to include `build-tools/libraries` as part of the BuildToolsApi domain. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21c39fa2d5dc4aeaf407b04334d4e888da88087dee4dbada10efcc7922b89120R174) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4281766c30d0d9309056e1801459aae9dee21979b55999b8ea1a2cb13a3d36a6R177)

**5. Miscellaneous**
- Linked the new documentation in relevant places (e.g., CLAUDE.md, plugin READMEs) and clarified that there are currently no modules yet in the new structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ccf4f9d920e67c77d01fa2ceabf31749ee75274b21e3f837ddf2f63ceec37966R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-74209963b1935accbfee2e442b3504262f2af774b931f9a13ff68162e455be9cR1-R39)

These changes lay the groundwork for extracting and sharing build logic across Kotlin build tool integrations, improving modularity, testability, and code reuse.

body.title: [K/N] Use llvm-ar instead of libtool

With the release of XCode 27 libtool started to produce binary unstable outputs: it insters random bytes as paddings.
An alternative to libtool is llvm-ar. llvm-ar doesn't suffer from the random paddings bug. And is bundled with the llvm distribution which we control better than XCode.
All the non-apple platfroms already use llvm-ar tool to produce static archives. This commit replaces libtool with llvm-ar on apple platforms as well.

body.title: KT-91109 [Gradle] Limit kotlin.build.disable.regeneration.check to version-dependent generators
body.body:
This pull request introduces a new mechanism for handling version-dependent generators in the build system, allowing only those generators whose output depends on the Kotlin version to bypass the "Re-generation needed!" check during version branching. It clarifies documentation, updates task definitions, and ensures that the regeneration check is only disabled for eligible generators.

**Improvements to generator tasks and configuration:**

* Added a `versionDependent` parameter to the `generatedSourcesTask` function, allowing tasks to declare if their output depends on the Kotlin version. Only these tasks can skip the regeneration check when the relevant property is set. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aee00041863410962fd4188cd198ee17c44f2b78058f4be06408bef28e432e10R62-R64) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aee00041863410962fd4188cd198ee17c44f2b78058f4be06408bef28e432e10R74) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-aee00041863410962fd4188cd198ee17c44f2b78058f4be06408bef28e432e10R91) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-aee00041863410962fd4188cd198ee17c44f2b78058f4be06408bef28e432e10R107) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-aee00041863410962fd4188cd198ee17c44f2b78058f4be06408bef28e432e10R116-R118)
* Updated usages of `generatedSourcesTask` in various build scripts to set `versionDependent = true` for appropriate tasks, ensuring correct application of the regeneration check logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7d903b841ab84d0de7be555fcdb6a073581b70857afa609754d9785f7e9921eaL62-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fcab892df187c81e034ae2e666a0767a314d7c8e3c6cdcb14ee4f666292274bcL67-R68) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9b9a92f30a7e102b455adaefaeaf2d251e2cb564d1b7964edb25a751a00243f9R110)

**Documentation and messaging updates:**

* Clarified documentation in `GeneratorsFileUtil.kt` and `gradle.properties` to explain that only version-dependent generators can skip the regeneration check, and updated the build problem message to guide developers on correct usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0f4bf12ed3cbd8839b7812d8628f101107ed37afa1563ebee3ce7cd9dac63ebfL21-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0f4bf12ed3cbd8839b7812d8628f101107ed37afa1563ebee3ce7cd9dac63ebfL95-R95) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3d103fc7c312a3e136f88e81cef592424b8af2464c468116545c4d22d6edcf19L157-R159)

body.title: Hair: Fix crashes in irToHair and Lower
body.body:
These bugs were causing crashes in HaIR phases that come after `irToHair` (e.g. `Lower`).  

Four different bugs were found:

1. Lambdas of type `() -> Nothing` would create `Unreachable`, yet `visitReturnableBlock` would still make a `BlockEntry` with no incoming edges, and a `Phi` node that points to it. Later that `BlockEntry` gets removed, but `Phi` doesn't in cases where it's used by another `Phi` node (like in a merge after `if/else` block). 

2. While true loops with no `break` never exit, yet exit blocks are still built, reachable only through condition's false branch. After `If(True)` is folded, DCE sets that branch's control to `Unreachable`, and then `replaceValueUses` puts that control node into `Phi`'s value input.

3. `visitCheckCast` replaced `CheckCast` with its operand by killing it. But since its in a control chain, its neighbors were not connected to each other.

4. Lowering one node edits its arguments. That can make GVN merge another node that is still waiting in the worklist, which kills it. The loop on worklist can reach that node, try to lower it, but it crashes.

body.body:
To produce the IR it hands to its consumer, the JKlib compiler serializes the module into a KLIB, then deserializes and relinks it. This PR removes that round trip: the consumer now gets the IR produced by FIR2IR and the first-phase lowerings directly, through `K2JKlibCompiler.compileToIr`.

Those are now resolved directly against the current compilation, which is possible because the consumer always passes the full set of transitive dependencies.

This makes compilation faster, removes the last part of JKlib that depended on the K1 frontend, and fixes the tests that were failing only because of the deserialization.

body.title: KT-81560 [Analysis API] Don't log AST loading errors in stub-based tests
body.body:
`withAstLoadingAssertion` forbids loading the AST of a stub-based file via `PsiManagerEx.setAssertOnFileLoadingFilter`. On an AST access, `PsiFileImpl` then reports it via `Logger.error`. In tests, that's IntelliJ's `DefaultLogger`, which prints the error with its stack trace to stderr and then throws an `AssertionError`. LL stub-based tests expect this error and catch it in `computeAstLoadingAware`, so they pass, but each caught error still leaves a full stack trace in the test log: 629 traces, about 78,000 lines of stderr, in `LLSourceLikeStubBasedResolutionTestGenerated` and `LLSourceAnnotationArgumentsCalculatorTestGenerated` alone.

Throw a dedicated `AstLoadingAssertionError` from the filter itself. The platform calls the filter only in `PsiFileImpl.loadTreeElement`, right before reporting the access, so the error is thrown at the same point. Unexpected AST loading still fails the test, and the error's stack trace points to the access. `computeAstLoadingAware` and `AbstractClassIdTest` now recognize the error by its type instead of matching the platform's message prefix.

Muting `DefaultLogger` via `disableStderrDumping` instead isn't an option: it flips a global static flag, and analysis tests run concurrently, so it would also mute errors of other tests, and overlapping save/restore pairs could leave dumping disabled for the rest of the run.

^KT-81560

body.title: KT-90851 [KGP] Migrate CheckXcodeTargetsConfigurationTask from Gson to kotlinx-serialization
body.body:
This pull request refactors the Xcode project parsing logic in `CheckXcodeTargetsConfigurationTask.kt` to replace the use of Gson with kotlinx.serialization for JSON parsing. This change modernizes the code, improves type safety, and aligns with the project's serialization standards. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Migration from Gson to kotlinx.serialization:**

* Replaced all `Gson`-based deserialization with kotlinx.serialization, including updating all data classes to use `@Serializable` and `@SerialName` annotations instead of `@SerializedName`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL8-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL268-R279) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL336-R394)
* Introduced a new `pbxprojJsonReader` using `Json(KgpJson.default)` with lenient parsing, and added a `decode` extension function for decoding `JsonObject` instances.

**Refactoring and Cleanup:**

* Removed all `Gson` imports, parameters, and usages throughout the parsing logic and helper functions, simplifying function signatures and internal logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL8-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL218-R223) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL255) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL292-R308) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-fa9764a9abef5edc13044b6eee3b4ea9efc553f83a7778d8648c481949e810baL336-R394)
* Updated the logic for checking object types and decoding fields to use kotlinx.serialization idioms (e.g., `JsonPrimitive.contentOrNull`).

**Data Model Updates:**

* Updated Xcode project structure data classes to use kotlinx.serialization, and replaced Gson-specific field annotations with kotlinx equivalents.

These changes collectively improve maintainability, type safety, and consistency in how Xcode project files are parsed and handled in the Kotlin Gradle plugin.

body.title: KT-86829 [KGP] Migrate UKlib manifest serialization from Gson to kotlinx-serialization
body.body:
This pull request refactors the serialization and deserialization logic for uklib manifests, moving from manual JSON handling with Gson to a type-safe approach using Kotlin serialization. It introduces a new `UklibManifest` class to represent the manifest structure and updates all relevant code to use this new model, improving maintainability and reliability.

**Serialization/Deserialization Refactor:**

* Introduced the `UklibManifest` serializable class in `uklibs/serialization/UklibManifest.kt` to represent the manifest structure, along with helper methods for encoding and decoding manifests using Kotlin serialization.
* Replaced Gson-based manual JSON construction and parsing in both manifest writing (`SerializeMetadataFragmentsOnlyUklibManifest.kt`, `uklibSerialization.kt`) and reading (`uklibDeserialization.kt`) with the new `UklibManifest` class and its serialization methods. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-246c4d8ecc4407aa21e290052642854219bdaa92e7c8fa0b7ddcb2c9adf97329L3-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-246c4d8ecc4407aa21e290052642854219bdaa92e7c8fa0b7ddcb2c9adf97329L33-R31) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-78658589cfe145f9039c8c681945dcc1bc5cb9f316c7cf72592ddda3382290b7L8-L13) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-78658589cfe145f9039c8c681945dcc1bc5cb9f316c7cf72592ddda3382290b7L30-R26) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fa44daaa97a50d4a97fe8e303f720bff608c1bc41b41f72e4981d2fc6c91acL8-L16) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fa44daaa97a50d4a97fe8e303f720bff608c1bc41b41f72e4981d2fc6c91acL34-L80)

**Codebase Simplification and Safety:**

* Removed manual map building, sorting, and property casting in favor of strongly typed data structures, reducing boilerplate and the risk of runtime errors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-246c4d8ecc4407aa21e290052642854219bdaa92e7c8fa0b7ddcb2c9adf97329L33-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fa44daaa97a50d4a97fe8e303f720bff608c1bc41b41f72e4981d2fc6c91acL34-L80)
* Eliminated now-unnecessary utility functions for property extraction from maps in favor of direct access to serializable data classes.

These changes make the uklib manifest handling more robust, easier to maintain, and less error-prone by leveraging Kotlin's serialization capabilities.

body.title: [K/N] Don't read class protos when building cache class fields (KT-90643)
body.body:
Removes the per-class proto walk from `buildSerializedClassFields`. Nothing it computes has reached the output since 873df4c70f94 (KT-52512). The walk re-parsed the whole top-level class for every nested class, which made cache builds quadratic: 141 s → 11 s for a class with 2000 nested models.

Checks that go away, and why that's fine:
- **Duplicate proto field names:** the serialized fields come from the IR, and `ClassFieldsDeserializer` matches them by index, not name.
- **`findClass` locating the class in its parent's proto:** that proto is no longer used.
- **"An inner class must have at least one outer class":** already implied by `require(irClass.isInner)`.

**Testing.** This is a pure performance fix with no change in output, so no test can fail when it is reverted, and K/N has no compile-time performance tests. Existing coverage of class fields in cached libraries passes:
- **Box tests**, `FirNativeCodegenBoxTestGenerated` `InnerClass*`, `InnerNested*`, `Classes*` and `Ir$SerializationRegressions*`: 195 tests, with `-Pkn.cacheMode=STATIC_EVERYWHERE` and with `STATIC_PER_FILE_EVERYWHERE`. They include `innerClass/inheritanceMultipleModules3.kt` and `serializationRegressions/innerClassInEnumEntryClass.kt`.
- **`:native:native.tests:cachesTest`**, including the per-file IC suite: 129 tests.

body.title: [stdlib] Fix Native and Wasm rounding conversion boundaries
body.body:
Draft follow-up to #8294 for [KT-89074](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-89074). This description and the patch were prepared with AI assistance. This remains a draft pending the contributor's own explanation, as requested in the previous review.

Native and Wasm implement rounding conversions using `floor(x + 0.5)`. The addition can round a value just below a half-integer across the boundary (`0.49999999999999994.roundToLong()` returns `1`), or change an already integral value (`8388609f.roundToInt()` returns `8388610`).

The patch takes the floor first and increments it when the remaining fraction is at least one half. This keeps ties towards positive infinity, including negative ties. Existing NaN and range checks remain in place.

Common tests cover neighboring values around half-integers, integral values at the precision boundary, and conversion limits for both floating-point types. Float limit inputs use explicit bit patterns: the earlier test incorrectly assumed `Int.MAX_VALUE.toFloat()` produces 2^31 on JS. No JS implementation change is needed.

Validation of the current test source:
- JVM, both JS Node targets, and Wasm-JS: each MathTest run passed 35 tests with one existing skip. All six new test methods executed.
- Linux Native, with explicitly selected source-built stdlibs: 35 passed and one existing skip in default and optimized modes. The same tests against the pre-fix stdlib produce four failures.

The Native libraries were built at the preceding test-only and implementation commits; the implementation is unchanged in the current revision. This is targeted Native validation, not a fresh full distribution or full Native suite run. Current-revision macOS, Windows, and Wasm-WASI runs are not claimed.

[Commands, artifact provenance, and test reports](https://github.com/mole828/kotlin/blob/28079845d8d9c3fe84d35f7308de1cccc18a0094/contribution-notes/KT-89074/REVISION-2.md).

body.title: KT-73488: Generalize lazy resolution of fake declarations
body.body:
[KT-73488](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-73488), [KT-73481](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-73481)

Fake declarations (fake overrides, delegated members, Java enhancement and synthetic properties, typealiased and SAM constructors) are created by scopes, do not belong to any FIR tree and share their content with the original declarations. Previously each lazy resolver skipped some of them on its own, typealiased and SAM constructors were not covered at all, so they were transformed by all resolvers under their own lock while sharing annotations with the original declarations.

- The first commit adds lazy resolve tests which target typealiased and SAM constructors themselves (a typealias or a class under the caret provides them). A typealiased constructor of a generic class instantiation crashes there, so that test is ignored.
- The second commit handles fake declarations in one place of `LLFirTargetResolver`: `isFakeDeclaration` is an exhaustive `when` over origins, and such declarations are not transformed. There are no behavior changes.
- The third and fourth commits make typealiased and SAM constructors fake declarations. Typealiased constructors do not copy bodies, delegated constructor calls and contracts anymore, and their default values are stubs as in fake overrides; SAM constructors are created in the same phase as fake overrides.
- The last commit stops resolving the original declarations of fake declarations: their signatures are already resolved, the shared annotations are resolved as foreign annotations, and a deferred return type is computed via the original declaration. Test data changes only in phases of the original declarations.

Callables imported from objects and wrapped integer operators are handled separately in KT-90592, as they share parameters with the original declarations.

Checked locally: the whole `:analysis:low-level-api-fir:test`, the LL diagnostics tests for the affected directories (typealias, SAM, j+k, override, substitutions, delegation, imports and others), FIR light tree diagnostics and JVM box tests for typealiases and SAM, and the Analysis API symbols, components and annotations tests.

body.title: [FIR] Make sure elements are actual subgraphs when collecting properties
body.body:
We currently check that an element could be used in the control-flow
graph of the container graph, but this check is not exact. It does not
distinguish between the instance and static graphs for a class. This
means a local property can be seen within the static graph container
which can cause false positive diagnostics.

After checking that the element could be part of the control-flow graph,
also check that it actually is part of the graph. This avoids the `null`
problems in the Analysis API while also being more exact.

^[KT-90674](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-90674) Fixed

body.title: Stdlib, JVM: Intercept TailCallBaseContinuationImpl
body.body:
Otherwise, tail-call suspend functions are undebuggable is most cases,
since the coroutine won't resume on a correct thread during
interception.

Now TailCallBaseContinuationImpl extends ContinuationImpl. It gets the
interception, the release and the context from ContinuationImpl.

The change is binary compatible. ContinuationImpl extends
BaseContinuationImpl, so the class keeps all its supertypes and public
members. The constructor does not change. The API dump shows no
supertype and no getContext, because BCV omits the internal
ContinuationImpl.
 #KT-90890 Fixed
